references.text: The verse describes how the Gibeonites prepared their deception with worn-out sacks and old wineskins, which connects to verse 5 where they also had worn shoes and clothes.
The Gibeonites explain themselves that their bread was warm when they left home, but now it had become dry, and the new wineskins had torn.
The Lord reminds Israel that their clothes did not wear out and their shoes did not fall apart during the journey in the wilderness, a contrast to the Gibeonites' claimed long journey.
Moses reminds the people that their shoes did not wear out from their feet during the wilderness journey, something the Gibeonites used as proof of a long journey.
Nehemiah also mentions how God ensured that shoes did not wear out during the wilderness journey, which provides background for the Gibeonites' deception.
